headline: UK judge sides with Russia on estoppel in Yukos Capital case
summary: An English judge has ruled that Russia is not prevented from pleading sovereign immunity as a defence to enforcement of a US$5 billion Energy Charter Treaty award won by a former Yukos affiliate – as no issue estoppel could arise from a Swiss court decision that upheld the award.

headline: Survey: institution and arbitrator costs compared across Asia
Freshfields’ Saudi disputes head joins Three Crowns in Dubai
summary: Amani Khalifa has left her role as head of the Saudi Arabia disputes practice at Freshfields to join the partnership at Three Crowns in Dubai.

headline: Malaysian investor threatens India over enforcement delays
summary: A Malaysian infrastructure company has reportedly threatened to bring a US$125 million investment treaty claim against India, alleging that judicial delays have prevented it from collecting on an arbitral award issued 12 years ago.

headline: Ukraine instructs boutique to defend US investor’s ICSID claim
summary: Ukraine has instructed European boutique Queritius to defend it in an ICSID claim brought by a US distressed debt investor that the state alleges is linked to Russia.

headline: EU lifts sanctions on Fridman
summary: The European Union has lifted sanctions on Russian-Israeli billionaire Mikhail Fridman, who has been pursuing investment treaty claims against western states that have frozen his assets.

headline: Russia loses Singapore immunity appeal in Yukos saga
summary: The Singapore Court of Appeal has upheld an order allowing the former majority shareholders of Yukos Oil Company to enforce awards now worth more than US$66 billion against Russia, finding the state’s immunity defence was precluded by transnational issue estoppel.

headline: Libyan state entity fails to lift French attachment
summary: A Kuwaiti company seeking to enforce a billion-dollar award against Libya has persuaded a Paris court to uphold an attachment of assets belonging to the state’s national oil company.

headline: AAA president joins Clio
summary: Bridget McCormack, who next month will step down as president and CEO of the American Arbitration Association, has joined legal AI company Clio to help expand the use of its technology in the judiciary.

headline: Ghana liable in desalination plant dispute
summary: A Spanish construction company says it has won US$235 million in an ICC dispute with Ghana and a state utility over a desalination plant in Accra.

headline: Emergency arbitrator rules in Albanian airport dispute
summary: An ICC emergency arbitrator has issued an interim order in a dispute over Albania’s termination of an airport concession, which is also the subject of a threatened ICSID claim.

headline: Reid leaves Debevoise for 3VB
summary: Natalie Reid has left Debevoise & Plimpton, where she was co-chair of the firm’s public international law group, to join 3 Verulam Buildings.

headline: Willkie names two new practice heads
summary: Willkie Farr & Gallagher has named Kristen Young in Washington, DC, as global co-chair of international arbitration and Dharshini Prasad as London chair of the practice.

headline: Construction arbitration in the Philippines
summary: The Philippine construction arbitration sits at the intersection of rapid infrastructure growth, mandatory CIAC jurisdiction and evolving procurement rules. With courts reinforcing CIAC’s authority despite parties’ chosen forums, foreign investors and contractors face important questions over party autonomy, enforcement risk and the balance between specialist domestic dispute resolution and intern...

headline: Nigeria beats Burford-backed hydropower claim
summary: Nigeria says it has defeated an ICC claim worth more than US$680 million brought by a power company funded by Burford Capital, which arose out of the purported settlement of a prior arbitration over a hydropower project.

headline: Spanish-Korean consortium wins award over biomass plant
summary: A Spanish-Korean consortium has won a net sum of €120 million in a London arbitration with the owner of a UK biomass power plant over a construction contract that was terminated during the covid-19 pandemic.

headline: Nokia win confirmed by court in Iranian telecoms case
summary: An award in favour of a French mobile company now owned by Nokia will stand, after a Paris court rejected allegations that an arbitrator was conflicted and death threats against witnesses were overlooked in a politically sensitive ICC dispute over a telecommunications project in Iran.

headline: Italy seeks to annul Veolia award
summary: Italy has applied to annul an Energy Charter Treaty award that required it to pay €86 million to French environmental services group Veolia for breaching two waste treatment concessions.

headline: Australian firm hires from Kennedys in Singapore
summary: Karnan Thirupathy, who is representing Swiss commodities trader Gunvor in an LCIA dispute over delayed LNG deliveries, has left Kennedys in Singapore to join Australian firm Wotton Kearney, bringing Charlene Sim with him.

headline: Romania avoids damages in wind farm dispute
summary: An ICSID tribunal has ruled that a Cypriot investor should receive no damages for changes to Romania’s renewable energy incentive scheme even though some of the measures violated the Energy Charter Treaty.

headline: Experts survive challenge in renewables case
summary: Expert witnesses from Compass Lexecon and FTI Consulting have survived a challenge to their credibility in a renewables case at ICSID based on their alleged financial dependence on cases referred to them by King & Spalding.

headline: Green fertiliser company threatens ICSID claim against Paraguay
summary: A London-listed fertiliser company has threatened to bring an ICSID claim against Paraguay after the state scrapped a fixed pricing regime for a “zero-carbon” ammonia plant.

headline: Canadian investor to file ECHR claim in Tunisian dispute
summary: A Canadian energy company that lost a US$130 million ICC claim against Tunisia says it will bring a complaint before the European Court of Human Rights, alleging that the presiding arbitrator failed to disclose her participation in conferences also attended by the state's counsel.

headline: YPF investors launch ICSID claim against Argentina
summary: Former investors in Argentina’s nationalised oil and gas operator YPF have made good on their threat to file an investment treaty claim against the state after a US$16 billion US court judgment in their favour was overturned.

headline: Paris institution launches mining group
summary: The Paris International Arbitration Chamber (CAIP) has launched a working group on arbitration in the mining sector co-chaired by Aboubacar Fall of AF Legal in Senegal and Baptiste Rigaudeau of French disputes boutique Lead Up.

headline: Delhi court to consider non-disclosure in Mozambique mining case
summary: Two companies have applied to a Delhi court to set aside what they say is an incorrectly decided partial award on joinder in an ICC case over a Mozambique coal mine, alleging that the Malaysian president of the tribunal, Sundra Rajoo, failed to disclose a relevant past appointment and quashed criminal proceedings against him.

headline: Omani conglomerate seeks to revive claim over joint venture
summary: An Omani conglomerate has asked a Dubai court to set aside an ICC award that rejected its US$55 million claim against an Indian home appliances company over their failed joint venture.

headline: Snellman disputes head joins Swedish firm
summary: Pontus Ewerlöf has left his role as head of dispute resolution at Snellman to join GAR 100 firm Gernandt & Danielsson as a partner in Stockholm.

headline: Russian lawyers launch London boutique
summary: Valeriya Grebenkova, who is advising Russian-Israeli billionaire Mikhail Fridman on several sanctions-related treaty claims, has launched a new boutique in London with transactional lawyer Angelina Golosova.

headline: Turkish contractor enforces against Georgia
summary: A US judge has agreed to enforce an ICC award requiring Georgia to pay over US$350 million to a Turkish construction group over a hydroelectric project that stalled because of public protests.

headline: Hong Kong panel orders education group to perform buyout
summary: An HKIAC tribunal has issued a final award requiring a Hong Kong-listed education group to perform a US$325 million buyout of its partners in a Cayman entity that operates schools and colleges in China.

headline: Baker McKenzie names new practice head
summary: Baker McKenzie has named London-based partner Kate Corby as its new global head of international arbitration, following the recent departure of Andy Moody.

headline: Paul Hastings completes hire of team from White & Case
summary: Anaïs Harlé and Opeyemi Longe have left White & Case to join Paul Hastings as of counsel in Paris and London respectively, two months after Elizabeth Oger-Gross and Tolu Obamuroh made the same move.

headline: “Space Odyssey” theme for next year’s IA Charity Ball
summary: The countdown to the 2027 International Arbitration Charity Ball is officially underway, as the organising committee reveals the theme for the event will be “Space Odyssey”.

headline: South Korea seals win in dispute with Chinese real estate investor
summary: A Chinese businessman has lost his bid to revive a US$192 million ICSID claim against South Korea over a real estate venture that was found to be part of an illegal financing scheme.

headline: Ex-White & Case partner launches UAE boutique
summary: Julia Zagonek, who previously led the Eastern European and CIS disputes team at White & Case before leaving last year, has launched a new firm in the Abu Dhabi Global Market.

headline: Ex-King & Spalding lawyer returns to Mattos Filho
summary: Caio Gabra has rejoined Brazilian firm Mattos Filho as a partner in São Paulo after three years at King & Spalding in the Middle East.

headline: ICC YAAF names regional reps
summary: The ICC Young Arbitration and ADR Forum for under-40s has announced 116 new regional representatives, bringing together its largest and most geographically diverse group to date from 87 cities in 73 countries.

headline: Award surfaces in Mexican quarry dispute
summary: A NAFTA tribunal found Mexico liable for “grossly unfair” conduct towards a US investor’s limestone quarrying operations while ordering the state to pay just US$16 million, a newly published award shows.

headline: Mexico defeats parking investor’s claim
summary: An ICSID tribunal has dismissed a US parking investor’s legacy NAFTA claim against Mexico on jurisdictional grounds.

headline: McCormack to step down as AAA president
summary: Bridget McCormack is stepping down as president and CEO of the American Arbitration Association to focus on the use of artificial intelligence in the judiciary.

headline: Holland & Knight wins tender to defend Ukraine in ICSID claim
summary: Holland & Knight has won a tender to defend Ukraine in an ICSID claim filed by an Austrian company that was sanctioned by the state amid allegations its founder paid taxes to Russia.

headline: Singapore boutique hires from Reed Smith
summary: Joyce Fong has left her role as counsel at Reed Smith to join Singaporean energy and commodities boutique Blackstone & Gold as a director.

headline: Italian contractor wins damages over Cameroon stadium project
summary: An Italian construction group has reportedly won an ICSID award worth more than €81 million against Cameroon over a troubled sports stadium project and alleged harassment by local authorities.

headline: Lima liable for terminating highway concession
summary: The Peruvian municipality of Lima has asked a US court to set aside an UNCITRAL tribunal’s finding that it unlawfully terminated a highway concession – the latest round of a fractious dispute that has already seen awards worth US$200 million and a pending ICSID claim.

headline: Panel in place for Fridman sanctions claim against UK
summary: Spanish arbitrator Miguel Virgós is chairing the UNCITRAL tribunal that will hear Russian-Israeli billionaire Mikhail Fridman’s investment treaty claim against the UK over the freezing of his assets due to sanctions.

headline: French Arbitration Association president goes solo
summary: Marc Henry, president of the French Arbitration Association, has founded his own boutique practice in Paris after a long career in law firms.

headline: DIS40 gains new co-chairs
summary: The German Arbitration Institute’s under-40 group, DIS40, has appointed three new co-chairs: Luiza von Croy from Bird & Bird, Alexander Monro from Freshfields and Greta Körner from King & Spalding.

headline: Russian LNG producer’s award upheld in Singapore
summary: A Baker Hughes subsidiary has failed to overturn a SIAC award that found it failed to mitigate the effect of sanctions on a contract to supply equipment to Russia’s largest LNG project.

headline: Moody leaves Baker McKenzie for Travers Smith
summary: Andy Moody has left Baker McKenzie in London, where he was global chair of international arbitration, to join the partnership at UK firm Travers Smith.

headline: Armenia hit with claim over “political” asset seizure
summary: A Belarusian-Russian businessman has made good on his threat to file an investment treaty claim against Armenia over what he calls a politically motivated seizure of his assets.

headline: Ukrainian state entity accuses arms dealer of frustrating LCIA case
summary: A Ukrainian state-owned defence company pursuing a US$347 million LCIA claim against a US weapons exporter has accused it of engaging in a corporate restructuring to frustrate enforcement of a future award.

headline: King & Wood hires from Debevoise in New York
summary: Nawi Ukabiala, who recently helped a Japanese mining company win a US$140 million ICSID award against Peru, has left Debevoise & Plimpton to join King & Wood as of counsel in New York.

headline: Russian appeal court affirms LCIA awards against Rusal are not enforceable
summary: A Russian cassation court has affirmed that LCIA awards worth more than €250 million won by a German bank against Russian aluminium group Rusal cannot be enforced.

headline: Oil trader wins HKIAC award over Indian deliveries
summary: An HKIAC tribunal has reportedly awarded more than US$100 million to an oil trader in a dispute with a Turkish company over oil deliveries to India.

headline: WFW hires construction partner in Dubai
summary: Construction disputes lawyer Guillaume Hess has joined the partnership at Watson Farley & Williams in Dubai.

headline: Top German court upholds enforcement against Libya
summary: UPDATED WITH COUNSEL: Germany’s Federal Court of Justice has upheld the enforcement of a £16 million ICC award won a decade ago by a US arms manufacturer against Libya over a contract for an army force led by former president Muammar Gaddafi’s son.

headline: Ukraine may face new claim over Fridman-linked seizure of drinks company
summary: The family of a deceased Georgian billionaire have threatened international legal action against Ukraine after the state froze a drinks company in which they hold shares alongside sanctioned Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman.

headline: Port operator settles with Uruguay
summary: A Chilean port operator has agreed to withdraw its US$600 million ICSID claim against Uruguay over the state’s decision to extend the concession of a rival terminal operator.

headline: Estonian agency files claim over Ukrainian artillery contracts
summary: An Estonian government agency has launched an ICC claim to recover €59 million in advance payments made to an Indian-owned supplier under EU-funded contracts to procure artillery shells for Ukraine.

headline: Peter & Kim makes double hire in Seoul
summary: Peter & Kim has hired Jin-uk (Joseph) Kim from Lee & Ko and Joonhak Choi from Kim & Chang to join the partnership in Seoul.

headline: Dominican Republic defeats waste management claim
summary: The Dominican Republic says it has defeated an investment treaty claim worth more than US$100 million brought by a French businessman over a waste management concession.

headline: Orlen pursues Petrofac over Lithuanian refinery project
summary: A subsidiary of Poland’s Orlen is seeking €104 million in an arbitration against embattled UK energy services group Petrofac over a terminated billion-euro contract to modernise Lithuania’s sole oil refinery.

headline: Peter Leaver KC 1944-2026
summary: Peter Leaver, an English silk who was chief executive of the Premier League in the 1990s and more recently chairman of the LCIA board and a leading commercial and sports arbitrator, has died aged 81.

headline: Finland and France fail to knock out ICSID claims
summary: An ICSID tribunal has refused to throw out a claim brought by an investor in Finland’s largest electricity distributor, as France fails to dismiss a Russian-Armenian billionaire’s case at the centre over the seizure of his assets.

headline: Korean shipbuilder defends another SIAC claim over cancelled Russian contract
summary: A Korean shipbuilder says it is facing a new SIAC claim worth US$1 billion brought by the operator of a Siberian LNG project over a contract that was terminated due to sanctions.

headline: Japanese mining company wins damages in Peruvian tax claim
summary: An ICSID tribunal has ordered Peru to pay more than US$140 million to a subsidiary of Japan’s Sumitomo Metal Mining over retroactive tax demands – two years after the investor’s US partner lost a claim over related measures.

headline: Naftogaz seizes Russian ship in Arctic
summary: Ukraine’s Naftogaz has persuaded Norwegian authorities to seize a Russian cruise vessel in the Arctic as it seeks to enforce a US$5 billion investment treaty award.

headline: Bondy goes solo
summary: Christophe Bondy, who led Canada’s defence against several high-profile NAFTA claims before joining Steptoe & Johnson, has left the firm to launch an independent arbitrator practice.

headline: Russian fintech investors launch claim against Uzbekistan
summary: A Russian fintech entrepreneur and his company have filed a US$100 million ICSID claim against Uzbekistan over a joint venture with the country’s national bank to launch a “buy now, pay later” payment card.

headline: Indus Waters Treaty still in force, rules panel
summary: A panel of lawyers and engineers has ruled that the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force despite India's insistence that it is "in abeyance" following an attack on tourists in Indian-administered Kashmir – meaning that an arbitration over hydroelectric projects on the river Indus and its tributaries continues.

headline: King & Spalding continues expansion with Paris hire from Quinn Emanuel
summary: Thomas Voisin has left Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan to join the partnership at King & Spalding in Paris, becoming the firm’s ninth international arbitration partner hire in the last three months.

headline: Ex-Morrison & Foerster practice head joins Crowell & Moring
summary: Chiraag Shah, the former global head of international arbitration and head of the Africa desk at Morrison & Foerster, has left the firm to join Crowell & Moring in London.

headline: Leaver passes away at 81
summary: Peter Leaver KC, the former chairman of the London Court of International Arbitration and a leading arbitrator at One Essex Court, has died aged 81.

headline: Italian engineering group wins damages in ammonia plant dispute
summary: Italy’s Maire says it has secured a €260 million ICC award in its dispute with a Russian fertiliser producer over an ammonia plant disrupted by sanctions.

headline: China beats bulk of Singaporean investor’s mega-claim
summary: An UNCITRAL tribunal has rejected a Singaporean businessman’s US$20 billion treaty claim against China over his lost real estate investments – but ordered the state to pay US$70 million that was owed under an earlier compensation agreement.

headline: Last former Hanotiau & van den Berg partner reveals plans
summary: Maarten Draye, the last former partner of Hanotiau & van den Berg to announce his plans after the Brussels arbitration boutique shut its doors last year, has formed an independent practice as arbitrator and counsel.

headline: Pinsent Masons hires from WilmerHale in Dubai
summary: Shanelle Irani has left her role as counsel at WilmerHale in London to join the partnership at Pinsent Masons in Dubai.

headline: LCIA panel issues award in Indonesian LNG dispute
summary: UPDATED. An LCIA tribunal has ordered a subsidiary of Indonesia’s national energy company Pertamina to pay damages to Swiss commodities trader Gunvor in a US$130 million claim over delayed LNG deliveries.

headline: Amirfar draws lessons from "disaggregated" proceedings
summary: Catherine Amirfar has pointed to the multiple "disaggregated" legal proceedings arising from the Qatar blockade and war in Ukraine, and to the non-binding ICJ advisory proceedings on climate change, to highlight the importance of arbitration and its sister mechanisms for managing and resolving geopolitical crises.

headline: Cast list emerges for Senegal-Morocco African Cup case
summary: GAR has uncovered the counsel and arbitrators appointed to hear Senegal’s bid at the Court of Arbitration for Sport to overturn a decision that stripped it of the Africa Cup of Nations title and awarded it to Morocco.

headline: Comparing arbitration costs in the Asia-Pacific
summary: Mark Mangan and Marcus Ho of Lindsay Francis Mangan & Lee compare the arbitrator and administrative fees charged by six leading arbitral institutions in the Asia-Pacific, highlighting significant differences in their pricing structures and the services the fees cover.

headline: Albania faces duo of claims over unfinished airport
summary: A Swiss company owned by Kosovo’s former president has threatened to file an ICSID claim against Albania over a cancelled concession to build an airport – as the concessionaire says it will pursue a separate LCIA case.

headline: Polasek envisages dispute prevention future for ICSID
summary: In the Maxwell Lecture in Singapore, ICSID secretary general Martina Polasek discussed how the 60-year old centre can "deepen its impact", suggesting that arbitration will remain central to its mission but the next chapter of its history may see more mediation and dispute prevention.

headline: Slovakia wins default enforcement of ICSID costs award
summary: A US court has granted Slovakia default enforcement of US$1.8 million owed by a Texan oil and gas company under an ICSID costs award after it lost a treaty claim over a drilling project.

headline: Practitioners weigh in on US appeal over non-signatories
summary: A group of practitioners and academics has urged the US Supreme Court to find that federal law, rather than state law, governs whether non-signatories can use equitable estoppel to enforce arbitration agreements under the New York Convention.

headline: Arbitrating construction disputes in Latin America
summary: Latin America’s construction projects range from multibillion-dollar infrastructure undertakings to smaller, locally funded ventures. Navigating this rich tapestry demands a thoughtful approach to arbitration as the preferred dispute resolution mechanism. However, the region's arbitration process is far from homogeneous. As Latin America continues to evolve and develop, the role of arbitration in ...

headline: Why arbitration is a smart choice in Latin America’s evolving legal landscape
summary: Latin America is emerging as a confident arbitration hub, backed by modern legal frameworks, pro-enforcement courts and growing acceptance of public-sector disputes. As jurisdictions align with international standards and strengthen party autonomy, businesses and investors gain clearer routes to efficient, predictable and enforceable dispute resolution across the region.

headline: Localising cross-border disputes: the growing appeal of regional arbitral centres in Latin America and the Caribbean
summary: Latin America’s arbitration market has moved from scepticism to sophistication, with regional centres increasingly handling larger, more complex and cross-border disputes. As institutions modernise rules, expand arbitrator rosters and embrace tools such as expedited procedures, emergency measures and third-party funding, arbitration users face a fast-evolving landscape shaped by innovation, local ...

headline: Arbitrating energy disputes in Latin America
summary: Latin America’s energy transition is reshaping investment risk as renewable incentives, fossil fuel phase-outs, political shifts and infrastructure constraints fuel increasingly complex arbitration. From Peru and Guatemala to Mexico and Chile, evolving regulatory regimes are creating uncertainty for states and investors alike, while opening new opportunities in one of the region’s most strategical...

headline: The New York Convention in Latin America
summary: Latin America remains a broadly pro-enforcement region for foreign arbitral awards, but practitioners must navigate a patchwork of national laws, treaty choices and constitutional remedies. From New York Convention reservations to amparo -style challenges and recent court decisions, enforcement strategy demands close attention to local procedure, public policy arguments and jurisdiction-sp...

headline: Methods for presenting expert evidence
summary: Expert evidence in international arbitration has evolved with frameworks such as the IBA and Prague Rules, balancing party-appointed and tribunal-appointed experts. Key challenges include expert selection, report drafting and witness preparation. Innovations such as hot-tubbing enhance efficiency but require careful management to ensure neutrality, credibility and procedural fairness.

headline: Enforcement of awards in Latin America
summary: While Latin American jurisdictions have taken diverse paths to the recognition and enforcement of international commercial arbitral awards, there is a trend towards uniformity. Despite the persistence of myths portraying Latin American countries as seats in which enforcing awards can be very challenging, these instances are more the exception than the rule.

headline: Expert reports and expert witness testimony
summary: As Latin American arbitration disputes become more technical and high-value, expert evidence is increasingly central to tribunal decision-making. From selecting credible, independent experts to producing rigorous reports and withstanding cross-examination, parties must navigate complex strategic choices. Strong expert input can clarify technical and financial issues and may ultimately determine wh...

headline: Causation before quantum: reframing damages analysis in arbitration
summary: Damages analysis in arbitration is often treated as a valuation exercise once economic harm has been assumed. A more robust approach asks first whether the loss being valued has been causally isolated from other economic forces that may have produced the same outcome.

headline: An overview of Brazil’s arbitration landscape
summary: Brazil has consolidated itself as a regional arbitration hub. This outcome has been driven by the efforts of the Brazilian arbitration community to promote arbitration, active arbitral institutions, legislation aligned with international standards, adherence to the New York Convention and the development of supportive case law. However, as in most jurisdictions, challenges remain, especially conce...

headline: Recent trends in ICSID awards involving Latin American states
summary: Latin American investment arbitration is entering a new phase, shaped less by sweeping nationalisations and more by mining, environmental regulation and community conflict. Recent ICSID decisions expose sharp divisions over state duties, investor expectations, security exceptions and damages, with outcomes turning on treaty wording, evidentiary records and how tribunals balance investment protecti...

headline: Shining a light on 30 years of successful arbitration law and practice in Mexico
summary: With 30 years of legislation and experience, Mexico now boasts a strong arbitration legal framework and thriving commercial practice. Against this backdrop, arbitration is on the brink of exponential growth due to imminent judicial reforms. While these may appear to weaken arbitration as a dispute resolution method, they could ultimately drive greater use and reliance.

headline: Introduction: growth, enforcement and emerging challenges in international arbitration in Latin America
summary: Latin America has cemented its status as one of the most important regions in the world for international arbitration, driven by rising case volumes, sophisticated regional institutions and increasingly arbitration-friendly courts. This fifth edition of GAR and Latin Lawyer’s The Guide to International Arbitration in Latin America , which draws on the expertise of highly soph...

headline: Venezuela defeats claim by dual national dairy investors
summary: A divided UNCITRAL tribunal has declined jurisdiction over a US$1.2 billion third-party funded treaty claim brought by three dairy investors because of their dual nationality.
